newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends slightly down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends slightly down in dull trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed slightly lower after another uneventful session due to lack of fresh consumer interest, dealers said.
"The market remains in the doldrums. There's nothing to report, not even inquiries," said one local dealer.
Another dealer said cheaper rubber in Thailand and Indonesia was pulling buyers away from the local market. "Prices have to come off further in order to become competitive again," she said.
Dealers, however, believed that further downside would be limited.

They said the Chinese Lunar New Year and Eid al-Fitr festivities in mid-February, when tapping stopped for nearly a week, and the onset of wintering, could put a strain on supply of latex to the market.

At the close, February RSS1 buyer was quoted at 303.50 cents ($1.22) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down half cent from Tuesday. February SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 300 cents ($1.20) a kg.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 298 cents a kg, SMR CV at 360, SMR L at 3404, SMR 5 at 310, SMR 10 at 299 and drum latex FOB at 235.
